annotation.authors_or_issuer: Gunkel, D.J.; Gerdes, A.; Coeckelbergh, M.
key_provisions_or_claims: Asks when robots might merit moral or legal standing, derived from Stone's 'Should Trees Have Standing?'
Essays debate electronic personhood, functional legal subjectivity, and gradient personhood as alternatives to the person/thing dichotomy
Navon proposes a Maimonides-based 'virtuous servant owner' intermediate status
Surveys show lay support for robot rights depends on perceived capacities, with only about one third endorsing personhood for sentient AI
Studies reveal a conflict between the urge to punish AI and legal systems
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Editorial introducing a Frontiers in Robotics and AI Research Topic on whether social robots should have moral or legal standing. It summarizes fifteen contributions on legal personality, public perception, and suffering-based status, and frames robot standing as relevant to anticipatory technology governance.
annotation.title_clean: Editorial: Should Robots Have Standing? The Moral and Legal Status of Social Robots
annotation.title_en: Editorial: Should Robots Have Standing? The Moral and Legal Status of Social Robots
